"''So, if it's a riddle, what's the question?|Ezra Bridger and Kanan Jarrus|}} '''Malachor''' was a rocky, hellish wasteland [[planet]] located in the [[Chorlian sector]] of [[the galaxy]]'s [[Outer Rim Territories]] region. It was a planet shrouded in mystery, and the location of an event known as the [[Great Scourge of Malachor]], which took place thousands of [[Standard year|years]] before the rise of the Empire. The Great Scourge was an ancient battle at Malachor's [[Sith]] [[Malachor Sith Temple|temple]] between the Sith and the [[Jedi Order]], which saw a [[Malachor superweapon|superweapon]] activated, [[Death|killing]] and petrifying all the participants of the battle, remaining for years after. During the [[Imperial Era]], [[Jedi Master]] [[Yoda]] told [[Ezra Bridger]], a [[Padawan]], to find Malachor to help him defeat [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] and the [[Inquisitorius|Inquisitors]]. Bridger, alongside [[Kanan Jarrus]] and [[Ahsoka Tano]], traveled to Malachor, where they found the former Sith Lord [[Maul]] in exile. Together, they killed three Inquisitors, but Maul blinded Jarrus and escaped, consumed by revenge against the Jedi as well as his [[Sith Master]], [[Darth Sidious]]. In the chaos, the Malachor superweapon was nearly re-activated before being destroyed, and while Bridger and Jarrus also fled Malachor, Tano narrowly survived her duel with Vader; years later, Bridger [[World Between Worlds|reached]] through the fabric of space-time to save Tano from Vader's clutches during the duel. With Tano spirited away, Vader departed with his armor scarred by battle, and Tano later [[Portal|returned]] to the duel's aftermath in order to continue her journey under Malachor's surface with the guidance of [[Morai]]. ==Description== {{Quote|Malachor is a lifeless planet remembered as the site of the Great Scourge—a battle that annihilated countless members of the Sith Order.|Darth Sidious|''[[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Sith]]''}} [[File:MalachorSurface.png|thumb|left|225x225px|The desolate surface of Malachor]] A slate-[[Color|gray]] desolate world of rocky wastes, Malachor was a bleak{{AtomicMassGames|url=character/i-am-no-jedi-duel-pack/|text=SWP42 I Am No Jedi Duel Pack|archivedate=20250731010722}} and barren [[planet]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories]], located in the [[Chorlian sector]]'s [[Malachor system]]. It had two dead [[moon]]s. The planet had a [[Malachor Sith Temple|Sith temple]] located underneath its surface, which resembled an [[ocean]] of liquid [[carbonite]] that had flash-frozen. Small, pyramidal, solid [[stone]] foothills were located equidistant from each other on the surface of the planet. Along Malachor's central latitude was a large crater ringed by narrow spires. The planet had perpetually thick [[cloud]]s and a breathable [[atmosphere]], though its air was stale and pungent. ==History== ===Early history=== {{Dialogue|Kanan Jarrus|Malachor has always been off-limits to Jedi.|Ezra Bridger|Why?|Kanan Jarrus|Old legends. Stories told to us as younglings in the temple.|Ahsoka Tano|There's always a bit of truth in legends.|attr=Kanan Jarrus, Ezra Bridger, and Ahsoka Tano discuss Malachor|src=}} [[File:Great_Scourge_of_Malachor_aftermath.png|thumb|right|230x225px|Ancient Jedi and Sith were left petrified on Malachor.]] At some point, the [[Sith]] were able to establish a presence on the planet Malachor, constructing a massive [[Sith temple|temple]] beneath its surface which was a place of worship and learning. This temple held a colossal [[kyber crystal]] that was used to power the temple and its [[Malachor superweapon|superweapon]]. Thousands of [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Cold War|brewing war]] between the [[First Order]] and the [[Resistance]], the planet was the location of a massive [[Great Scourge of Malachor|battle]],''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]'' in which the [[Jedi Order]] launched an all-out assault against the [[Sith Empire|Sith]]. During the battle, the temple's weapon misfired and petrified everyone on the planet. After these events, Malachor was made forbidden to the [[Jedi]], though stories of what had happened were passed down, forming the basis of many legends. Millennia later, the debris of war still littered the battlefield. Any traces of the planet's existence were erased in the [[Jedi Archives]], in the hopes the Sith secrets could be completely lost.''[[Unlimited Power]]'' For millennia, the world was off-limits, with tales and dark legends of the world told to [[Jedi Initiate]]s. However, many [[spacer]]s claimed to have found the planet and would bring back Sith relics; some were obvious frauds, but others had genuine connections to the [[Dark side of the Force|dark side]]. [[Smuggler]]s also claimed to make [[Ashes of Malachor]], made from the pulverized bones of those who fought there. These ashes empowered those who consumed it—increasing their might, but at the cost of morality. Along with the Sith worlds of [[Jaguada]], [[Rhelg]], and [[Ziost]], Malachor was quarantined during the [[Republic Era|time]] of the [[Galactic Republic]].''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' ===Fall of the Republic=== {{Quote|It was here on... on this dead world... that the Jedi struck a terrible blow against the Sith. Many of our order were struck down. All because they wanted to be ''free''.|Darth Sidious, to Maul|[[Darth Maul (2017) 2|''Darth Maul'' (2017) 2]]}} [[File:Malachor-AORDarthMaul1.png|thumb|left|225x225px|Maul and Sidious explore the site of the battle]] The [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth Sidious]] traveled to Malachor at one point and experienced a vision of the Sith of lore.{{StoryCite|story=Disturbance|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}} At one point, Sidious took the former [[Nightbrothers|Nightbrother]] [[Maul]] as his [[Sith apprentice|apprentice]], the two of them traveled to Malachor. There, Sidious showed Maul a [[Force vision|vision]] of the battle between the Sith and the Jedi. Later, both Sith returned to Malachor, where Sidious showed Maul yet another vision, in which Maul became a Jedi but betrayed those he was helping. Sidious used this to teach Maul that Sith must not act without thinking about their actions.[[Age of Republic - Darth Maul 1|''Age of Republic - Darth Maul'' 1]] The visions were the result of inhaling the ash of dead [[Force-sensitive|Force-users]]. On another occasion, Sidious visited Malachor and acquired a [[Darth Sidious' Sith Chalice|Sith Chalice]]. Due to its infamy, Malachor was often invoked as a curse word. While contemplating his strategy for getting himself and his [[D-Squad|team]] of [[astromech droid]]s off the [[desert]] world of [[Abafar]], [[Colonel]] [[Meebur Gascon]] exclaimed that there was "no way in Malachor" that he would lead his team on an [[Escape from Abafar|assault]] on a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist]] landing field.{{TCW|Missing in Action}} Years later, during the [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], the [[crime lord]] [[Cikatro Vizago]] of the [[Broken Horn Syndicate]] used Malachor as an epithet while working with the smuggler [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]].{{InsiderCite|158|Rebel Bluff}} ===Age of the Empire=== ====A quest for knowledge==== {{Dialogue|Ezra Bridger|If Malachor is off limits, why would Master Yoda send us here?|Kanan Jarrus|I don't know, but I trust Master Yoda. There's something here for us.|Ezra Bridger|Yeah, something to help us stop the Inquisitors.|Ahsoka Tano|Knowledge.|attr=Ezra, Kanan, and Ahsoka discuss their mission|src=}} [[File:AhsokaKananandEzraarriveonMalachor.png|thumb|right|260px|Ahsoka, Kanan, and Ezra arrive on Malachor]] During their rebellion [[Early rebellion against the Galactic Empire|against]] the Empire, three rebels—the Jedi [[Kanan Jarrus]] and [[Ezra Bridger]], along with [[Ahsoka Tano]], a former Jedi—traveled to the [[Lothal Jedi Temple|Jedi Temple]] on [[Lothal]] to seek the spectral guidance of [[Jedi Master]] [[Yoda]] in the hopes of defeating the Sith [[Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] and his [[Inquisitorius|Inquisitors]]. Yoda told Bridger that, if he and the others wanted to fight, they had to find Malachor.{{Rebels|Shroud of Darkness}} After helping the [[Phoenix Cell]] establish a [[Chopper Base|base]] on [[Atollon]], Jarrus, Bridger, and Tano [[Mission to Malachor|traveled]] to Malachor together.{{Rebels|The Mystery of Chopper Base}} On Malachor, the two Jedi and Tano discovered a deep chasm which led to an ancient Sith temple. There, the three friends were attacked by an Inquisitor known as the [[Eighth Brother]]. Bridger was separated and fell into a tunnel. There, he encountered the former Sith Lord Maul, who also wanted to defeat the Sith. Maul befriended Bridger and the two joined forces to venture into the temple in order to find the "secret" that could destroy the Sith. Working together, the two retrieved a [[Sith holocron (Malachor)|Sith holocron]] from the temple. Bridger and Maul then reunited with Jarrus and Tano, who were being attacked by the Eighth Brother, the [[Fifth Brother]], and the [[Seventh Sister]]. After Maul drove the Inquisitors away, Maul convinced Bridger and the others that they had to enter the Temple in order to activate the [[Sith holocron|holocron]]. He claimed that doing so would give them the knowledge they needed to destroy the Sith. The Inquisitors soon caught up with them. While Jarrus and Tano fought with the Inquisitors, Maul sent Bridger to bring the holocron to the top of the temple. Meanwhile, Maul [[Death|killed]] the Inquisitors before turning on Jarrus and Tano. He blinded Jarrus but was stopped by Tano. While Jarrus pushed Maul off the cliff, Tano went to deal with Bridger. Meanwhile, Bridger planted the holocron into the temple's obelisk. He encountered a [[Presence|female voice]] who revealed that the temple was an ancient Sith [[Malachor superweapon|superweapon]] capable of destroying all life. Bridger refused to use the Temple's knowledge and was attacked by [[Darth]] Vader, who had arrived in [[Darth Vader's TIE Advanced|his]] [[TIE Advanced x1|TIE Advanced starfighter]]. [[File:Master_versus_the_apprentice.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Ahsoka Tano battles her former master, now Darth Vader, on Malachor.]] Tano arrived to rescue Bridger and began [[Lightsaber duel|duel]] with Vader while Jarrus and Bridger joined forces to remove the [[holocron]]. As the temple was building up a power charge, the removal of the holocron caused it to implode. Jarrus and Bridger managed to escape before the temple closed in on them, but they were unable to help Tano, who ensured that her companions escaped before returning to her duel with Vader in the collapsing temple. Tano fought against her former master, refusing to leave him despite Vader's intent to slay his former apprentice. ====Aftermath==== {{Quote|Ahsoka?''"
"''Ezra? You look... Wait, what happened? Where am I?''"
"''You were fighting Vader. I saw you in there. He was going to... So I... I grabbed you, and I pulled you out of there.|Ezra describes his rescue of Ahsoka to her|{{Rebels|A World Between Worlds}}}} Jarrus and Bridger were recovered by Chopper, and the three departed the world minus their companion Tano. Maul, who had survived the fall, eventually fled the planet using one of the fallen Inquisitors' TIE Advanced v1s. [[File:A-World-Between-Worlds.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Ahsoka was rescued from Malachor by Ezra via the World Between Worlds]] As Vader and Tano's duel continued, Vader began to overpower her. As he prepared the fatal blow, Tano was pulled away from the collapsing temple into the [[World Between Worlds]] by Bridger and the [[Force wielder]]-related [[convor]] [[Morai]], surviving the event. Tano was confused how she had departed Malachor and did not know where she was, but Bridger explained to her what had happened. Later, Tano departed the World Between Worlds and returned to Malachor, walking into the Sith temple. Before the convor left the temple,{{SWCT|set=Artist Series - Dave Filoni|cardname=9 (Ahsoka Tano)}} Morai guided Tano through the temple's flooded depths{{SWCT|set=Artist Series - Dave Filoni|cardname=7 (Ahsoka Tano)}} so she could reach another portal to the World Between Worlds.{{SWCT|set=Artist Series - Dave Filoni|cardname=10 (Ahsoka Tano)}} Meanwhile, a wounded Darth Vader had escaped the temple before it collapsed, limping away from the ruins while being observed by Morai. The Sith Lord would be recovered by an Imperial cruiser. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|There is a place in the galaxy where the dark side of the Force runs strong. It is something of the Sith, but it was fueled by war. It corrupts all that walks on its surface—drowns them in the power of the dark side. It corrupts all life, and it feeds on death.|Darth Traya speaks of Malachor V in ''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords''|audio=KreiaMalachorV.flac|''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''}} [[File:MalachorV.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Malachor V, as it appeared in ''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords'']] In [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]], [[Malachor V]], as it was known in that era, was a planet that was first referenced in the [[2003]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''. The game revealed that it was the location of the [[Battle of Malachor V]], the final battle between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], led by [[Revan/Legends|Revan]], and the [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]] during the [[Mandalorian Wars]].''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' The world went on to appear as the final location in the sequel, ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'', revealing that it was a shattered and ruined world consumed by the energies of the [[Mass Shadow Generator/Legends|Mass Shadow Generator]]. This event led to a pyrrhic victory for the Republic, destroying many Mandalorian and even Republic forces in the process. In ''The Sith Lords'', Malachor V housed the [[Trayus Academy]], an ancient [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] academy used by the [[Sith Triumvirate]] of [[Kreia|Darth Traya]], [[Darth Nihilus]], and [[Darth Sion]] in the aftermath of the [[Jedi Civil War]]. The Jedi Exile, [[Meetra Surik]],''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]'' traveled to the Trayus Academy, where she defeated Sion and Traya during the game's final levels. The name Malachor was later used as an expletive by Meebur Gascon in "[[Missing in Action]]," an episode of the animated television series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', which, after the 2014 canon reboot, remained in official Star Wars [[canon]]. ==Appearances== *{{StoryCite|story=A Life Immortal|book=Dark Legends}} {{Mo}} {{Flash}} *[[Darth Maul (2017) 2|''Darth Maul'' (2017) 2]]
